newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Diana takes anti-mine campaign to Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Diana takes anti-mine campaign to Bosnia.

text.p: Britain's Princess Diana took her campaign against land mines to Bosnia on Friday, meeting victims wounded by the weapons left over from the country's devastating war.

Diana paid her first visit to a Bosnian mine victim in the north-east town of Tuzla, where she spoke for 45 minutes with Franjo Kresic, a former soldier who lost his leg in a mine blast during the country's 1992-95 war.
The princess emerged from the rundown apartment block smiling and waving at neighbourhood children who gathered to greet her.
Diana, looking deeply tanned and fit, beamed as she patted the children on the head and shook their hands as they chanted "Diana! Diana!"

She gave a cold stare to reporters when they asked her to confirm British newspaper accounts linking her to film producer Dodi Fayed, son of Egyptian tycoon Mohammed Al-Fayed, who owns London's' luxury department store Harrods.
The divorced princess, trying to promote her role as a roving humanitarian ambassador, planned to highlight the plight of mine victims in a three-day "private visit" to Bosnia.

Lord Deedes, a writer and friend of Diana's, said the princess stopped in the central town of Olovo en route to Tuzla, where she got a first hand look at reconstruction efforts to repair damage done by wartime shelling.
Deedes said Diana had shown a keen interest in the suffering caused by the war and was not allowing the media frenzy to distract her.
"Since she got here, she has been totally self-possessed. The princess has a knack of putting her mind on what she is doing," Deedes said.
"Whatever other distractions are, she puts her mind on what she's doing. She is in excellent form."

Dressed in a pale blue shirt, blue blazer, cropped blue jeans and suede flat pumps, Diana later met the mayor of Tuzla, Selim Beslagic, known for promoting co-existence among Bosnian Moslems, Orthodox Serbs, Roman Catholic Croats.

Diana's white private Lear jet touched down earlier on Friday as a gaggle of press waited on the tarmac of Sarajevo airport, once the scene of vicious fighting between rival armies during the Bosnian conflict.

On the morning of her departure, British tabloids were full of speculation about Diana's friendship with 41-year old Fayed and said she had been seen entering his luxury London apartment for a dinner date.
The Daily Mail's front page headline read: "Diana -- it's a real romance", while The Sun said: "Romantic meal in new love's London flat -- then farewell kiss before Bosnia".
Her 15-year marriage to British royal heir Prince Charles ended in divorce last year.
Diana, 36, was invited to Sarajevo by the Washington-based Landmine Survivors' Network, which tries to raise funds for mine victims and to promote a ban on the weapons.

It is the second time Diana has visited a former war zone on her anti-mine campaign. The first trip, to Angola in January, brought home to many around the world the terrible toll inflicted on civilians by the millions of anti-personnel mines left behind by war.

Diana was not expected to visit Serb-controlled territory in Bosnia, where anti-British feeling is running high following an operation by British special forces to arrest two Serbs wanted for war crimes which resulted in one of them being shot dead.
